test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 04 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'** i.e. **'But'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure **"not only... but also"** is a common correlative conjunction used to emphasize that both parts of the statement are true. 
 
• **Even without** the** "also**," "but" often pairs with "not only" to draw attention to the second part of the statement, suggesting that it might be surprising or unexpected in the context of the first part.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"I am proud to belong to a religion which has taught the world both tolerance and universal acceptance," he declared on September 11, 1893. "We believe not only in universal toleration, **but **we accept all religions as true. I am proud to belong to a nation which has sheltered the persecuted and the (5) _________ of all religions and all nations of the earth."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yet:** This word often signals a contrast or an unexpected turn, but it doesn't pair naturally with "not only" in this context.
 
• **Though:** Similar to "yet," "though" could signal a contrast, but it's not the standard word used to pair with "not only." It doesn't provide the same clear emphasis that "but" does.
 
• **And:** This conjunction doesn't emphasize the surprising or unexpected nature of the second part of the statement in the way that "but" does. It simply links the two parts without adding any particular emphasis or contrast.
